Tile-level concurrency for raster reads

Source: R/concurrency.R
a5px_set_concurrency.Rd

a5px's reader runs as a producer / consumer pipeline:

Usage

a5px_set_concurrency(cpu_workers = NULL, io_concurrency = NULL)

a5px_get_concurrency()

Arguments

cpu_workers

Integer scalar (>= 1) or NULL.

io_concurrency

Integer scalar (>= 1) or NULL.

Value

a5px_set_concurrency() returns the previous setting invisibly. a5px_get_concurrency() returns a list with the current resolved defaults.

Details

  • cpu_workers is the number of CPU threads a read uses: the blocking-thread consumers that decode each block, and the pool of the same size that indexes each decoded block as row stripes, so a read that spans fewer blocks than workers still uses every worker. Pick this to match the number of physical cores you can spare.

  • io_concurrency is the number of remote requests a read keeps in flight, across all its sources. Blocks next to each other in the file (a band's blocks along a row, say) are fetched in one request. For local files it is the number of blocks read at once.

These two knobs replace the old threads arg, which conflated tokio worker count and tile-level parallelism in confusing ways.

Defaults are resolved per call: function args > options > env vars > built-in default. For cpu_workers that is the number of CPUs available to the R process, which respects affinity masks and container or cgroup CPU quotas (a job limited to 4 CPUs on a 20-core host gets 4); for io_concurrency it is 32. Set globally via a5px_set_concurrency(), options(a5px.cpu_workers = ...), options(a5px.io_concurrency = ...), or environment variables A5PX_CPU_WORKERS / A5PX_IO_CONCURRENCY.

Examples

a5px_set_concurrency(cpu_workers = 8, io_concurrency = 32)
a5px_get_concurrency()
#> $cpu_workers
#> [1] 8
#> 
#> $io_concurrency
#> [1] 32
#>
